[FACT] User practices martial arts.  
[PREFERENCE] User wants to improve flexibility for martial arts.  
[CHANGE] User does not have a lot of time to spare for warming up and stretching.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stretch regularly: incorporate stretching into your daily routine to gradually increase flexibility.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Use dynamic stretching: warm up with light exercise like jumping jacks or lunges, and add dynamic stretches such as leg swings or torso twists.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Include static stretches: after dynamic stretching or martial arts practice, hold a position for 30 seconds or longer to help increase flexibility.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Incorporate yoga or pilates: adding these can greatly improve flexibility and strengthen the core.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Consult a professional: work with a martial arts instructor or personal trainer to develop a tailored stretching routine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stay consistent: flexibility takes time to improve, so consistency is key.  
[USER] User expresses intent to try to make time for stretching outside of martial arts practice to avoid injuries.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Prioritizing stretching and warming up is a great way to prevent injuries and improve performance in martial arts.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Consistency is key; even a few minutes each day can make a big difference.  
[USER] User asks for specific stretching routines or videos tailored for martial arts training.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant cannot provide specific links or videos but suggests popular stretching exercises for martial arts:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Hip stretches: hip circles, lunges, pigeon pose, butterfly stretch.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Quadricep stretches: quad stretch, standing leg swings, front split stretch.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Hamstring stretches: forward fold, downward dog, hamstring stretch.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Shoulder stretches: shoulder circles, arm circles, shoulder stretch.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Core stretches: cat-cow stretch, bridge pose, seated twist.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Gradually increase range of motion and hold each stretch for at least 30 seconds.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Always warm up muscles first and never force the body into painful positions.
